gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on an OBC-era Club Car DS or Precedent the on-board computer sits between the charge port and the batteries. Bypassing it turns off all of its functions. Lester's bypass kit (CGR-123, $127.99) gives back the 'cart locked out while the charger plug is in' function only with a compatible Lester charger. So a generic lithium kit charger plugged into a bypassed cart has no stated drive lockout, and the bypass kit's price can push the Vatrer kit past $1,700.
standout_why: I compared against our own page (dealectric.com/best-48v-lithium-golf-cart-battery-kit-with-charger-club-car), which ChatGPT cited. It already says OBC carts from about 1995 to 2014 need a bypass, but it says nothing about a drive lockout and lists no bypass-kit part or price. I also checked cartvolts.com/carts/club-car/precedent-2014-plus/, which covers the 3-pin receptacle, ERIC charging and some 2014 carts keeping an OBC, but has no lockout or bypass-kit cost. All seven ChatGPT answers say only that an 'OBC bypass may be needed'. I could not open the Vatrer product page or Vatrer's OBC guide (403), and I did not open golfcartgearlab.com or cartvoltage.com.
decides: This matters only for owners of an OBC-era DS or Precedent (about 1995 to 2014). For them the bypass is a real cost and it changes how the cart behaves. Lester CGR-123 at $127.99 plus the Vatrer Club Car kit at $1,579.99 (Dealectric's recorded price, not rechecked today) comes to $1,707.98, which is over the $1,700 cap. LiTime at $1,281.66 (litime.com, 2026-11-03) plus $127.99 comes to $1,409.65, which is under. The page should also tell these owners that, after a bypass, keeping a drive lockout while charging depends on the charger's plug. Lester documents it only with its own compatible charger. For 2014-and-later ERIC carts with no OBC, the Vatrer pick stands.

findings.label: What the bypass disables
findings.value: Once installed, 'all OBC functionality will be disabled, including the dash light'. The OBC no longer records charge and discharge history.
findings.source_title: Club Car Golf Cart Onboard Computer OBC Bypass Kit for Lester Chargers (Pete's Golf Carts)
findings.note: Retailer listing that repeats Lester Electrical's kit description. The kit is made by Lester specifically for Club Car DS and Precedent.

findings.label: Drive lockout after the bypass
findings.value: With a compatible Lester charger, 'vehicle lockout is also provided when the charger DC plug (Shelf unit) is connected to the vehicle charging receptacle'. For on-board chargers, the lockout happens when the AC plug is connected.
findings.source_title: Club Car Golf Cart Onboard Computer OBC Bypass Kit for Lester Chargers (Pete's Golf Carts)
findings.note: The lockout is described only for compatible Lester chargers. Nothing says a third-party lithium charger such as Vatrer's, LiTime's or Redodo's provides it.

findings.label: Fit limit
findings.value: 'Only Compatible with OBC carts that utilize the 6 Pin Deutsch Connectors'. It is for DS and Precedent models. OBCs are non-returnable.
findings.source_title: Club Car Golf Cart Onboard Computer OBC Bypass Kit for Lester Chargers (Pete's Golf Carts)
findings.note: The listing gives no model years.

findings.label: Price
findings.source_title: Club Car Golf Cart Onboard Computer OBC Bypass Kit for Lester Chargers (Pete's Golf Carts)
findings.note: Totals: Vatrer $1,579.99 + $127.99 = $1,707.98. LiTime $1,281.66 + $127.99 = $1,409.65. Both kit prices are from earlier Dealectric records, not rechecked today.

findings.label: Club Car charge circuit (PowerDrive, Club Car's own manual)
findings.value: 'The vehicle charge circuit consists of the charger receptacle, fuse link, onboard computer and the batteries'. 'The gray wire (sense lead) from the charger receptacle is connected to the sense lead fuse'. 'DO NOT BYPASS THE SENSE LEAD FUSE!'
findings.source_title: Club Car 1998 Maintenance and Service Manual Supplement (1998/1999 PowerDrive Plus), page 14-3
findings.note: Shows that the OBC sits in series between the receptacle and the pack, so a lithium charger plugged into the stock port charges through the OBC unless the OBC is bypassed. The manual covers 1998 and 1999 PowerDrive Plus carts.

findings.product: Epoch Club Car Precedent port plug
findings.label: Replacement charge port for an on-board lithium charger
findings.value: $32. A 110 V AC inlet (SKU EP-Receptacle-CC) that replaces 'the obsolete lead-acid charge port'. Listed for Precedent only. The listing does not mention a drive lockout.
findings.source_title: Club Car Precedent Port Plug | Epoch
findings.note: Epoch says the listing does not confirm fit for Onward, Tempo or DS.

findings.label: 2014-and-later Precedent charging
findings.value: 'No OBC, ERIC charging (some 2014 carts still have an OBC)'. 'Round 3-pin Club Car 48V receptacle'. 'Your receptacle may not match the new charger.'
findings.source_title: Club Car Precedent 2014+ Lithium Conversion Kits | CartVolts
findings.note: This is a rival page in ChatGPT's results. It is listed here to mark what rivals already cover.
